title: Lower your heart rate before sleep: Bryan Johnson's #1 health tip and HRBS protocol
summary: Bryan argues heart rate before sleep (HRBS) is the single most important health metric and a longevity lever, because it predicts sleep quality. He explains how to measure it, what a good score is, and gives a protocol of food, caffeine, exercise, stress and light habits that lowers it.

principles.text: If you focus on one health thing, lower your heart rate before sleep.
principles.quote: But if you're going to focus on one thing, it would be this: Lower your heart rate before sleep.

principles.text: HRBS is a single-number biomarker of fitness, metabolic health, food habits and stress management.
principles.quote: HRBS is a powerful biomarker of overall health. A single number representing how your whole body is doing.

principles.text: Lower HRBS means faster, deeper sleep, and sleep is the #1 longevity therapy.
principles.quote: This is critical because sleep is the #1 longevity therapy.

principles.text: Measure HRBS lying flat for 60 seconds; use a wearable or count the pulse for 15 seconds and multiply by 4. Around 50 bpm is great.
principles.quote: If you don't, count your pulse for 15 seconds and then multiply by 4

principles.text: His HRBS predicts his sleep quality: around 40 bpm gives a perfect night, 57 bpm costs about 30% of sleep quality.
principles.quote: If it's 40 bpm, I am guaranteed a perfect night's sleep. If it's 57 bpm, I'll lose about 30% of my sleep quality.

principles.text: Finish food about 4 hours before bed, avoid heavy meals and alcohol, and end caffeine by 12pm.
principles.quote: Finish all food ~4 hours before bed (earlier the better)
